sketches.title: Site Sabotage
sketches.premise: You are a building site trying to finish a job while your rival keeps throwing hazards at the plan. On each turn, place one site problem that directly wrecks the problem now on top; the chain ends when your fix fails.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that your standing site problem directly causes, blocks, breaks, or makes impossible the previous one; merely avoiding it, waiting it out, making a larger copy, or naming a related nuisance loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name one site thing and its action in one sentence: “I am a power cut: I shut down the drill that is boring through my floor.” The host says, “A brave little blackout—nothing says progress like standing in the dark.”
sketches.first_card: I am a concrete mixer, churning across the access road.

sketches.title: Blueprint Brawl
sketches.premise: Two rival foremen alter one shared building plan, one change at a time. Your change must make the latest feature impossible to build while keeping your own sentence clear enough for the crew to follow.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that your alteration physically or logically prevents the previous plan feature; a detour, delay, duplicate feature, or vague “I redesign it better” does not count.
sketches.move_shape: State one plan change and the exact clash: “I move the only staircase into the wall, so the new upper floor has nowhere to reach.” The host notes, “Excellent architecture: a staircase for people who enjoy becoming plaster.”
sketches.first_card: The plan puts a glass wall across the front of the building.

sketches.title: Toolbox Takedown
sketches.premise: You and your opponent run a cursed toolbox in a worksite showdown. Each turn, choose one ordinary tool or material that makes the last one useless for its stated job; the first useless choice loses.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the new tool or material directly stops, jams, cuts, melts, absorbs, or otherwise defeats the previous one in a plain worksite use; dodging it, outlasting it, or choosing a bigger version of the same tool loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name the item, its job, and the takedown: “I am a magnet, pulling the nails out of the hammer’s wooden handle.” The host says, “The hammer has been promoted to an expensive stick. Proud day for the toolbox.”
sketches.first_card: I am a nail gun, firing nails into a timber frame.

sketches.title: Crew Command
sketches.premise: Two site bosses issue one order at a time to a crew that obeys the latest clear command. Give an order that makes the previous order impossible or self-defeating, without simply reversing it or shouting louder.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that your command directly prevents the crew from carrying out the standing command; “do it later,” “do it more,” a mere refusal, or an unrelated order loses.
sketches.move_shape: Give one short order with its interference: “Send the safety inspector to lock the ladder before anyone climbs it.” The host says, “At last, a management strategy: deploy paperwork until gravity wins.”
sketches.first_card: Crew, carry this steel beam through the narrow doorway.

sketches.title: Material Meltdown
sketches.premise: A building material sits at the centre of a feud, and each player names the next ordinary material that ruins its useful job. Keep the failure specific: the new material must act on what is there, not merely sit nearby looking smug.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the new material directly cracks, dissolves, soaks, burns, seals, or otherwise defeats the previous material in a recognizable building use; hiding, surviving, or using a thicker cousin loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name one material and its effect: “I am water, soaking the cardboard box until it collapses.” The host says, “The box has discovered its natural enemy: basic weather.”
sketches.first_card: I am fresh wet paint, covering the bedroom wall.

sketches.title: Site Rumour
sketches.premise: You are rival site managers trying to control one dangerous rumour about the job. Each turn, add a plain fact that makes the current rumour impossible, not merely less likely; the first fact that fails to break it loses.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that your fact directly contradicts or removes the condition making the standing rumour true; ignoring it, adding a bigger rumour, or offering a metaphor instead of a mechanism loses.
sketches.move_shape: State one fact and the contradiction: “The rumour says the lift works, but the building has no lift shaft, so it cannot run.” The host says, “A devastating revelation: the elevator is not hiding; it was never invited.”
sketches.first_card: The site rumour is: “The new roof is already keeping the rain out.”
